description: Gate for `rag bench` on PostgreSQL with RAG_VECTOR_SEARCH=approximate (ADR-0014; CI runs it at 10,000 chunks with --requests 0 --pdf-pages 0). It checks the HNSW index itself: recall against exact search over golden v2's questions, measured with the index plan forced, since at this size PostgreSQL rightly prefers an exact scan; index_used_rate fails the gate if the search can no longer use the index at all. Calibrated with hashing-v1-d512, m 32, ef_construction 128, ef_search 200 on pgvector 0.8.6: two runs gave recall 0.9908 and 0.9904 (lowest question 0.8667) and the same first result for 0.9894. HNSW builds are randomized, so the minimums leave room. No regression rules: there is no baseline for this configuration.

query.latency_ms.retrieval.p95.source: requirements 7: retrieval p95 under 300 ms at 10,000 chunks

query.vector_recall.index_used_rate.source: every compared search read the HNSW index
